## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured the title by beating Inter 5-0 in the final, a run powered by elite offensive output where they ranked higher than 97% of that season's teams in both Attacks per game and Shots per game. The club also outperformed 94% of their peers in Passes per game and 92% in Pre-season UEFA club coefficient points, establishing a dominant statistical profile among the 24 knockout participants.

## Would the model have picked them?
Although the model assigned a 10.1% probability of reaching the final—exceeding the 8.3% base rate for a random team—it ranked only eighth among all knockout teams, meaning it did not select Paris Saint-Germain as a top-two finalist. The calculated expected stage of 0.82 places them nearest to the quarter-finals on the scale, indicating that while they were a leading contender in reality, the model trained on historical data viewed them as significantly less likely to reach the summit than the actual outcome suggests.

## Weak spots
The team's least impressive metrics relative to their peers were Long passes (% of passes) at 17%, Shot accuracy (% on target) at 33%, and Shot conversion (% of shots scored) at 26%. Despite ranking well in these areas, the model marked down Long passes as a negative factor with a SHAP contribution of -0.15, while simultaneously penalizing their high Opponent shots per game despite them beating 94% of teams on that stat.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat drove, propelled, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
